overview:
Josh Gottheimer, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a northern New Jersey district that only modestly favors his party. He enters the general election with an enormous financial advantage, more than thirteen million dollars on hand, while Republican Sean Kirrane has raised under one hundred thousand dollars and has little cash remaining. Betting markets on both major platforms put the Democratic chance at roughly ninety-six to ninety-seven percent.

No public general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals: the incumbent's history of comfortable wins, a modestly Democratic-leaning electorate, and a favorable national environment. The challenger has run a low-visibility campaign without meaningful outside backing. Unless outside money or a late shift in the national climate changes the picture, the seat is expected to stay in Democratic hands by a wide margin.
